rationale: Operator explicitly rejected Ctrl+B because the Ctrl+B -> Ctrl+V transition requires an uncomfortable pointer-finger stretch.

Ctrl+Space is selected by the implementation as the next ergonomic candidate because the scheduler chord uses the thumb for Space and leaves the index finger available for V; operator acceptance is still pending empirical trial.
Ctrl+B UT-10 recorded one extra hotkey press and one rejected submission despite 20/20 actions and durable acknowledgments.
invariant_preservation: browser adapter and content-blind security boundary unchanged
retention_gate: Retain Ctrl+Space only after zero unintended scheduler dispatches, zero required native shortcut collisions, and hotkey interference <=2/7 in representative work.
